details.value: "Transforming Clinical Diagnostics with PCR: From Microbiome Analysis to HPV Genotyping"

body.text: The African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases (ACEGID), Redeemer’s University, Ede, recently hosted a scientific delegation from CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health as part of activities associated with the programme titled:
“Transforming Clinical Diagnostics with PCR: From Microbiome Analysis to HPV Genotyping.”

The visit formed part of ongoing efforts to strengthen scientific capacity, institutional collaboration, and knowledge exchange in the areas of molecular diagnostics, pathogen genomics, infectious disease surveillance, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and One Health innovation.

The delegation was led by Professor Joseph Omololu-Aso, Professor of Infectious Disease and Climate Change Intervention at Obafemi Awolowo University and Director-General/CEO of CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health.

The visit was undertaken with the support and encouragement of Professor John Akíntúndé Ọládọ̀tun Òkèníyì, Chief Medical Director of Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospitals Complex (OAUTHC), under the growing collaboration framework involving CPM International Research Institute, Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), and OAUTHC.
Scientific Engagement and Facility Tour

Although the scheduled onsite workshop sessions did not proceed as originally planned, the visiting team was warmly received by representatives of Redeemer’s University and ACEGID and was provided an extensive guided tour of the Centre’s facilities.
The delegation had the opportunity to observe cutting-edge infrastructure supporting:
Advancing Climate-Health, Pathogenomics & One Health

The engagement is particularly relevant to ongoing efforts by CPM International Research Institute, OAU, and OAUTHC to strengthen climate-sensitive infectious disease surveillance and implementation science in Nigeria.

CPM International Research Institute, working in collaboration with OAUTHC and Obafemi Awolowo University, has commenced implementation activities under the Osun State Climate-Health Surveillance Pilot, serving as an emerging clinical demonstration platform for evidence generation and public health innovation.
Institutional Collaboration & Appreciation

Professor Joseph Omololu-Aso noted that exposure to world-class pathogenomics infrastructure remains essential for the development of sustainable national platforms capable of supporting disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness, precision public health, and translational research.

The visiting delegation expressed profound appreciation to the management and staff of Redeemer’s University and ACEGID for their hospitality, professionalism, and commitment to scientific leadership across Africa.
Strategic Highlights

items: Genomics Synergy: Bridging clinical diagnostics with high-throughput sequencing.
Osun State Pilot: Real-time climate-pathogen field data collection.
One Health Framework: Unifying clinical medicine, climate science, and public health.

body.text: The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health, Professor Joseph Omololu-Aso, on 13th April 2026 paid an official visit to the Palace of His Imperial Majesty, Oba Rashidi Adewolu Akanmu Ladoja, Olubadan of Ibadanland, as part of ongoing stakeholder engagement and strategic consultations on advancing climate-health innovation, infectious disease preparedness, pathogenomics, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and One Health research in Nigeria.
The visit was facilitated through the distinguished support of the Are Aago of Ibadanland, Rear Admiral Ibikunle Akintola (Rtd.), who graciously arranged the audience and accompanied the engagement.
Royal Audience and Strategic Discussions

During the meeting, Professor Omololu-Aso presented the vision of CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health, including ongoing initiatives in climate-sensitive infectious disease surveillance, pathogenomics, antimicrobial resistance research, One Health innovation, and public health preparedness.

Particular attention was given to the emerging concept of establishing an innovation and research hub that would contribute to scientific advancement, workforce development, disease surveillance, research capacity strengthening, and community impact within Ibadanland and beyond.
Royal Encouragement & Traditional Partnership

"His Imperial Majesty warmly received the delegation and expressed appreciation for initiatives aimed at advancing health, research, innovation, and human capacity development. The Olubadan encouraged the pursuit of impactful scientific and public health initiatives capable of benefiting Ibadanland, Oyo State, Nigeria, and the wider African region."
His Imperial Majesty assured the delegation of his goodwill, fatherly support, prayers, and openness to future engagements as the vision continues to develop.
Official Palace Audience Report Note

This report documents the official audience granted to Professor Joseph Omololu-Aso, Director-General/CEO of CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health, by His Imperial Majesty, Oba Rashidi Adewolu Akanmu Ladoja, Olubadan of Ibadanland, on 13 April 2026.
Photographs were not taken during this initial courtesy and strategic engagement. Future meetings and project activities will be documented as appropriate.
Palace Engagement Focus

items: Establishment of Innovation & Research Hub in Ibadanland
Role of Traditional Leadership in Public Health Preparedness
Centre of Excellence on Climate-Sensitive Diseases & AMR

title: OAUTHC-OAU-CPM Climate-Health Collaboration Takes Nigerian Research to Cambridge and Tanzania
summary: OAUTHC leadership under Professor John Akintunde Okeniyi advances clinical research, scientific mentorship and international engagement.

body.text: ILE-IFE, NIGERIA | October 2026

The collaboration between the Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospitals Complex (OAUTHC), Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), and CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health is gaining international visibility through emerging research opportunities for Mrs Adeola Victoria Anisere, an OAUTHC staff member, PhD student at OAU, and CPM International Research Institute’s focal person for the Osun State Climate Health Surveillance Pilot.

Mrs Anisere will present her research work at Epigenomics of Common Diseases 2026, scheduled for 4–6 November 2026 at the Wellcome Genome Campus, Hinxton, Cambridge, United Kingdom. Her accepted research, titled “From Environmental Exposure to Host Vulnerability: Establishing a Climate Health Intelligence Platform for Epigenomic Research in Nigeria,” explores a framework for investigating environmental exposures, host vulnerability and climate-sensitive health outcomes.
This milestone highlights the potential of Nigerian hospital-based research to contribute to international scientific discussions while addressing locally relevant public-health challenges.

Under the leadership of Professor John Akintunde Okeniyi, Chief Medical Director of OAUTHC, the Teaching Hospitals Complex provides an important clinical platform for collaborative research connecting patient care, surveillance and public-health innovation. The Osun State pilot, undertaken in collaboration with OAU and CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health, seeks to strengthen research on climate-sensitive respiratory and infectious disease risks.

Mrs Anisere is pursuing her PhD under the scientific supervision of Professor Joseph Omololu-Aso, Professor of Infectious Disease & Climate Change Intervention, Clinical Microbiology & Immunology at OAU and Director-General/CEO of CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health Ltd/Gte.

Professor Omololu-Aso’s research and institutional development initiatives focus on climate-sensitive infectious diseases, pathogenomics, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), One Health innovation and AI-enabled public-health surveillance. His mentorship reflects a commitment to developing emerging Nigerian researchers while building sustainable platforms for scientific collaboration and public-health impact.

Mrs Anisere is also expected to participate in the Hospital Partnerships Alliance (HPA) Global Forum in Moshi, Tanzania, from 8–11 November 2026, under the applicable HPA/GIZ-supported arrangements. This separate engagement offers further opportunities for professional exchange and collaboration on climate change and health.

The UK and Tanzania engagements underscore the value of connecting clinical research, postgraduate training and international partnerships. They also highlight the potential of the OAU–OAUTHC–CPM collaboration to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity for climate-health intelligence, infectious disease surveillance and evidence-informed public-health action.

CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health commends Professor Okeniyi’s institutional leadership, Professor Omololu-Aso’s scientific mentorship, and Mrs Anisere’s contribution to this developing research initiative.
About the collaboration:

The Osun State Climate Health Surveillance Pilot brings together OAU, OAUTHC and CPM International Research Institute for Climate Health to advance clinical surveillance and research on climate-sensitive health outcomes.

The initiative is strengthened by CPM’s signed Memorandum of Understanding with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), establishing a formal basis for institutional collaboration. Engagement with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), alongside federal-level support initiatives involving the Ministries responsible for Health, Environment and Education, forms part of the wider national framework for coordinated climate-health research and surveillance. CPM’s international collaboration with Philipps University Marburg, Germany, formalised through an MoU, further strengthens its research partnership network.

body.text: The CHIP™ (Climate Health Intelligence Platform) development team has announced a major milestone. The AI-enabled Climate Health Digital Twin is now entering final integration testing, with a beta release expected in Q3 2026. The platform will integrate climate data, disease surveillance, laboratory intelligence, and genomic data in real time.

seo.description: Climate Health Intelligence Platform nears completion with advanced AI capabilities for real-time surveillance.

title: CPM Int'l Hosts Regional Training Workshop on Genomic Surveillance
summary: Over 50 scientists and public health professionals participate in capacity-building initiative.

body.text: CPM Int'l successfully conducted a week-long training workshop on pathogenomics and genomic surveillance for researchers and public health professionals across West Africa. The workshop covered molecular epidemiology, sequencing technologies, and data interpretation for outbreak response.
